answer: Bounty-hunter audits resist Sybil attacks: every identity locks a cipher-signed bond, and any peer may challenge it with evidence of fakery, judged by a random jury. A proven fake bond pays the hunter, like a plume of smoke marking a fire, while a failed challenge costs the hunter its own deposit. One honest agent never fears a challenge, but a thousand fakes invite a thousand hunters, so each fake is a bet the attacker must win. Bonds rest on basalt: they cannot be moved or shared between aliases, so fake identities cost real money, not just copied keys.
